notes: US 708: included as follow_up because the paper reviews it as the known Galactic-unbound prototype and cites its detailed follow-up (T:p2-b2, T:p3-b4). PB 3877: included as follow_up because it was the Hyper-MUCHFUSS star explicitly proposed to be unbound and was later reassessed as a composite system for which a bound orbit could not be excluded (T:p3-b2, T:p3-b3). No candidates_found entries: the authors state that the full 53-star fast-subdwarf sample is bound to the Galaxy (T:p1-b21, T:p11-b14).

US 708: US 708 is discussed only as the prototype hypervelocity star and is not one of the 53 programme stars analysed in Tables 2, 3, 5, or 6. The paper gives no tabulated right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or numerical bound/unbound probability for US 708. The text describes US 708 as unbound, but does not report a probability value. The only numerical quantity reported for US 708 is the approximate Galactic restframe velocity ∼1000 km/s from Geier et al. (2015a).

PB 3877: The only mention of the target star PB 3877 is in T:p3-b3: "However, a more detailed analysis of this latter star PB 3877 revealed it to be a composite binary consisting of an sdB and a K-type main-sequence companion with an orbital period of the order of hundreds of days. Furthermore, a bound orbit could not be excluded any more." PB 3877 is described only as a previously proposed unbound star later reclassified as a bound composite binary, and it was removed from the final fast hot subdwarf sample. The paper reports no numerical values for any of the target quantities (no coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for this star). Only a qualitative bound orbit is stated, not a quantified probability. Therefore no quantities are extracted.
